verdicts.concept: DATE criteria field types and formats
verdicts.claim: DATE criteria supports five date format types: ISODATE (ISO-8601 formatted date, default), EPOCH_SECONDS, EPOCH_MILLIS, EPOCH_NANOSECONDS (all Unix epoch timestamps requiring BSON type long), and OBJECT_ID.
verdicts.evidence: Valid values: ISODATE, EPOCH_SECONDS, EPOCH_MILLIS, EPOCH_NANOSECONDS, or OBJECT_ID.

verdicts.concept: DATE criteria field types and formats
verdicts.claim: Time series collections only support ISODATE format for the date field value in DATE criteria.
verdicts.evidence: Source states you must set type to DATE if collection_type is TIMESERIES, but does not explicitly restrict to ISODATE.

verdicts.claim: MongoDB Atlas Online Archive DATE criteria supports exactly five date_format values: ISODATE, EPOCH_SECONDS, EPOCH_MILLIS, EPOCH_NANOSECONDS, and OBJECT_ID.
verdicts.evidence: Valid values: ISODATE, EPOCH_SECONDS, EPOCH_MILLIS, EPOCH_NANOSECONDS, or OBJECT_ID.

verdicts.claim: The date field used for archival criteria cannot be modified after the online archive is created.
verdicts.evidence: partition_fields ... cannot be modified after an Online Archive is created; changing partition structure requires deleting the archive and creating a new one with the desired fields.

verdicts.claim: MongoDB Atlas Online Archive calculates document age using the formula: current_date > dateField + expireAfterDays.
verdicts.evidence: MongoDB Cloud archives the data when the current date exceeds the date in this database parameter plus the number of days specified through the expireAfterDays parameter.

verdicts.claim: The bounds of 7 to 9215 days apply to dataExpirationRule.expireAfterDays, not to criteria.expireAfterDays.
verdicts.evidence: Number of days used in the date criteria for nominating documents for deletion. Value must be between 7 and 9215.

verdicts.concept: Partition fields constraints for DATE rules
verdicts.claim: For DATE criteria (Date Match), the date field used for archiving must be included as one of the partition fields and is positioned first by default.
verdicts.evidence: Source does not confirm 'must' or 'first by default' positioning, only lists allowed number of fields.

verdicts.concept: Partition fields constraints for DATE rules
verdicts.claim: When using DATE criteria, a maximum of three partition fields are allowed: the date field plus up to two additional commonly-queried fields.
verdicts.evidence: You can specify up to two frequently queried fields (or up to three fields when one of them is date_field) to use for partitioning data.

verdicts.claim: DATE criteria selects a single date field and an age in days; only the age parameter can be modified after archive creation, not the chosen date field.
verdicts.evidence: partition_fields ... cannot be modified after an Online Archive is created; changing partition structure requires deleting the archive and creating a new one with the desired fields.

verdicts.claim: Custom Criteria accepts standard MongoDB query filter expressions to define archival conditions.
verdicts.evidence: JSON query to use to select documents for archiving. Atlas uses the specified query with the db.collection.find(query) command.

notes: Source for Claim 6 (Terraform) explicitly mentions 'date criteria' for deletion, which contradicts the artifact's claim that 'criteria.expireAfterDays' is for archival and 'dataExpirationRule' is for deletion.
The 700 character limit for partition fields was verified as being applicable to all partition fields including the date field.
